title: Catch OverflowError in ByteSize validation
answers: Why does ByteSize raise an unhandled OverflowError on huge string values?
How to handle OverflowError when validating large string inputs in ByteSize?
ByteSize validation crashes on very large numbers instead of raising ValidationError
body:
Symptom: Validating a ByteSize field from a string with an excessively large numeric value crashes with an unhandled OverflowError instead of a ValidationError.
Root cause: pydantic/types.py:ByteSize converts the scalar using float(scalar) * unit_mult without catching float OverflowError.
Fix pattern: Wrap numeric string conversions in try/except OverflowError and reraise as PydanticCustomError to ensure proper ValidationError reporting.
Constraints: Applies to string parsing into float scalars; does not apply to direct integer inputs which support arbitrary precision in Python.
